svg.title: Gloobal — Backend Architecture (as built)
svg.desc: End-to-end architecture of the Gloobal platform: existing React PWA on Netlify, Express 5 API on Render, MongoDB Atlas. Verified against Backend/server.js, Backend/models, and the frontend source.
svg.text: As built and deployed, not proposed. Every box below was verified against Backend/server.js, Backend/models/, and the frontend source.
EXISTING FRONTEND — unchanged by this architecture
Precaches the app shell, so the
first visit after a deploy still
Only transport into the backend. No WebSocket, no GraphQL.
Named origins only — was cors() with
Bounds what one request can make
Request survives CORS, size and rate checks
HMAC-SHA256 bearer token · not a JWT library
Claims: sub (user _id), symbolId, iat, exp. Signature compared with
timingSafeEqual, length-checked first. Expired or unsigned → 401.
requireSelf — is it their own data
Reads the Gloobal ID from path, then body, then query, and compares
by document _id — never by symbolId string, so a rename mid-session
cannot lock someone out of their own account. Mismatch → 403.
CREDENTIAL STORES — what proves identity in the first place
Public routes skip this layer entirely (see below).
Validated inputs handed to the domain rules
Amount, identity and format checks already done.
BUSINESS LOGIC — where money is actually protected
Atlas is a replica set → yes.
Every write inside a transaction carries its session.
Replica set · multi-document transactions · db: gloobal_db
COLLECTIONS — 14 models, 12 written by the API
The only scheduled mechanism in the whole system is Mongo's TTL index on Otp.expiresAt. There is no application scheduler,
no queue and no worker process — see the asynchronous panel on the right.
Every route's catch block writes a
reports the comparison. The app shows
a red banner when they disagree.
Gap — no APM or error tracking
No Sentry, no structured logger, no
metrics, no alerting, no uptime check.
A 500 in production is visible only by
NOT IN THIS ARCHITECTURE — drawn so nobody assumes otherwise
No Redis, no Memcached. Rate buckets
live in process memory; every read goes
No BullMQ, Agenda or cron. Every unit of
work completes inside the request that
asked for it, or not at all.
No S3, no Cloudinary, no multer. Profile
photos are held in the browser's own
No SMS gateway, no push, no email from
the API. OTP is a fixed prototype code.
report-mailer is a separate local tool.
No WebSocket, no SSE, no polling loop.
The client learns about changes only by
The API server makes no outbound HTTP
calls at all. No webhooks in or out, no
Fetched by the browser, never by the server.
Each origin is allowlisted in the netlify.toml CSP.
Static SPA build, SPA rewrite to index.html,
Node 20 web service, auto-deploys on push
to main (~30 s). Free tier sleeps: cold start
20–50 s, which is why the client allows 45 s.
Single instance — see the rate-limit caveat.
Frontend and backend are separate checkouts
The existing client already speaks to every route drawn here.
Held in browser localStorage, so a photo does not follow
the account across devices. Adding object storage is the
one change that would require client work to upload.
There is no queue and no worker process.
The two mechanisms below are the entire story.
Expiry runs inside the database, not the app.
In-process, drops expired buckets. Not durable.
Response flow — JSON back to client
Declared in code but never used
Dashed borders mean "exists in the schema, carries no data".
Run against a throwaway database on the same
Atlas cluster, so transaction behaviour matches
production exactly. Dropped after each run.
Concurrent mints against one balance; concurrent
sends of the same coin; the three-way invariant
Ten concurrent sends of 800 against a balance of
1000. Written to fail against the pre-fix version,
which is how it was confirmed to detect the bug.
Token forgery and expiry, cross-account reads,
The client-side ledger is tested independently of
the server: books balance per currency, coin cannot
be added to fiat, reconciliation ignores junk.
Passkey and face flows, OTP delivery, the seed
migrations, and every screen's event handlers.
